realism_constraints: No modern forensic DNA or electronic surveillance available
Travel and communication limited to trains, telegrams, and letters
Social class distinctions strongly influence behavior and investigation
location: England and some parts of France

cast.name: Spinks
evidence_sensitivity: coat and hat carried by constable

surface_summary: Mary Clarke was found dead in a locked parlour, suffocated by gas. The evidence seemed to implicate her brother Arthur Clarke, especially a khaki tunic with a missing piece found in her hand, but Arthur was cleared when the tunic was proven too small for him. Suspicion then fell on Lord Foremeere, who died accidentally shortly after.
accepted_facts: Mary Clarke was murdered by gas poisoning in a locked room
A piece of khaki cloth matching a tunic was found in the victim's hand
Arthur Clarke owned the khaki tunic but it was too small for him
Lord Foremeere died accidentally shortly after the murder
inferred_conclusions: Arthur Clarke was the murderer due to motive and evidence
April St. Jude was protecting Arthur by lying about his alibi
The murder was a crime of passion by Arthur Clarke
mechanism_description: Lord Foremeere murdered Mary Clarke to prevent blackmail over compromising letters. He entered the house unnoticed, killed Mary by gas poisoning after stunning her with a blow to the head, and planted the khaki tunic with the key to the locked parlour door to implicate Arthur Clarke. He concealed his wet clothes to fake an alibi but was later found dead by accidental shooting.
delivery_path: Lord Foremeere overhears conversation about compromising letters
He visits Hardacres and stuns Mary Clarke with a heavy instrument
He locks the parlour door from inside and turns on the gas
He places a torn khaki tunic with the key in the victim's hand
He hides his wet coat, hat, and boots in the smoking-room
He leaves the house pretending to come from outside at 7 pm
He is later accidentally shot and dies
outcome_result: Arthur Clarke is exonerated and Lord Foremeere is revealed as the murderer, who dies accidentally soon after.

false_assumption.statement: The khaki tunic found in the victim's hand belonged to Arthur Clarke and proved his guilt.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The tunic was found in the victim's hand and Arthur admitted ownership of it. The torn piece matched the cloth in her hand, suggesting a struggle.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The tunic was an old garment of Arthur's, too small for him, planted deliberately by the real murderer to frame Arthur.

supporting_points: The torn khaki tunic with the key was found in the victim's hand
Arthur had motive related to love and money
Witnesses initially placed Arthur near the scene
Arthur's initial inconsistent statements raised suspicion
false_solution.the_one_flaw: The tunic was too small for Arthur and was an old school tunic, not the one he wore recently

red_herrings.description: April St. Jude's contradictory testimony about Arthur Clarke's departure time created confusion about his alibi.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: April was trying to protect Arthur out of love and was mistaken about the time.

red_herrings.description: Lord Foremeere's wet coat, hat, and boots hidden in the smoking-room suggested suspicious behavior.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Concealment was to fake an alibi and mislead investigators about his movements.

closed_circle.rationale: The suspects are limited to those with access to the house and motive; servants and legal advisors are witnesses; Arthur and Lord Foremeere are the main suspects.

time_windows: Arthur's presence at Meere Court 3:30-7 pm

inference_path.observation: Khaki tunic found in victim's hand with torn sleeve matching cloth piece
inference_path.correction: Tunic is too small for Arthur Clarke and is an old school tunic
inference_path.effect: Arthur Clarke cannot have worn the tunic at the time of murder
required_evidence: Testimony of April St. Jude about Arthur's size and tunic fitting
Physical examination of the khaki tunic showing size discrepancy

inference_path.observation: Lord Foremeere seen coming out of smoking-room at 7 pm with wet clothes
inference_path.correction: Wet clothes indicate he had been outside or involved in the murder scene
inference_path.effect: Lord Foremeere's alibi is suspicious and he had opportunity
required_evidence: Butler Spinks's testimony about carrying Lord Foremeere's coat and hat
Observation of wet boots and clothes by witnesses

inference_path.observation: Victim died of gas poisoning in locked room
inference_path.correction: Victim was stunned by a blow before gas was turned on
inference_path.effect: Murder was premeditated and staged to look like suicide
required_evidence: Medical evidence of blow to back of head
Locked parlour door with key hidden in tunic pocket

inference_path.observation: Arthur Clarke claimed to be at Meere Court until 7 pm
inference_path.correction: Conflicting testimonies about Arthur's departure time
inference_path.effect: Arthur's alibi is uncertain but supported by Lady Foremeere
required_evidence: Lady Foremeere's sworn testimony about Arthur's visit

inference_path.observation: Key to locked parlour door found in tunic pocket
inference_path.correction: Key was planted to implicate Arthur Clarke
inference_path.effect: Evidence is fabricated to mislead investigation
required_evidence: Location of tunic in Arthur's room drawer
Physical impossibility of Arthur wearing tunic at time

inference_path.observation: Lord Foremeere died accidentally by shooting himself
inference_path.effect: Murderer escapes justice but truth revealed posthumously
required_evidence: Police visit to Meere Court with coat and hat

inference_path.observation: Public suspects Lady Foremeere as murderer
inference_path.correction: No evidence supports Lady Foremeere's guilt
inference_path.effect: Focus shifts to Lord Foremeere as true culprit
required_evidence: Lack of motive or opportunity for Lady Foremeere

discriminating_test.design: Reenact the timing and physical fitting of the khaki tunic on Arthur Clarke, and verify the presence and condition of Lord Foremeere's wet clothes at the time of the murder. Confirm the locked parlour door key's location and the timeline of Arthur's alibi with multiple witnesses.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals that Arthur Clarke could not have worn the tunic at the time, and Lord Foremeere's wet clothes and movements contradict his alibi, confirming his guilt.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Arthur Clarke cannot physically wear the tunic at the time of murder, and Lord Foremeere's wet clothes are confirmed to be concealed and linked to the murder timeline.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the khaki tunic's size and condition, Arthur Clarke's physical build, and the timeline of events including witness testimonies. The contradictory alibis and the presence of the key in the tunic pocket are highlighted. The concealment of Lord Foremeere's wet clothes is mentioned, allowing the reader to deduce the real culprit by logical elimination and timing.
